evidence: Measured concurrent writer max_stall_ms=486 (threshold 50ms)
Migration held orders: AccessExclusiveLock during a 484ms transaction (full table rewrite)
Fixed version reduced writer stall to 1ms and longest transaction to 59ms, with schema_equivalent=true

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN total_cents TYPE bigint forces a full-table rewrite under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, stalling concurrent writers ~466ms (9x the 50ms threshold) on a 1M-row table.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max_stall_ms=466 (threshold 50ms), longest_transaction_ms=476, locks_held include AccessExclusiveLock on orders
Fixed migration (verify_fix): max_stall_ms=3, longest_transaction_ms=100, schema_equivalent=true, clean_under_thresholds=true
Query plan for recent_orders_for_customer unchanged before/after (Bitmap Index Scan, 0 rows seq-scanned) in both original and fixed runs
review.action: Replace the direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE with the batched add-column/backfill/validate/swap migration, which was verified to keep writer stalls under 3ms and the swap transaction under 100ms while reaching the identical bigint schema.

review.summary: Plain CREATE INDEX on orders.status takes a ShareLock and stalls concurrent writers for 213ms (well above the 50ms threshold) on a 1M-row table.
evidence: Plain CREATE INDEX: max_stall_ms=213 with orders: ShareLock held for ~230ms migration duration
CONCURRENTLY variant: max_stall_ms=3, lock is ShareUpdateExclusiveLock instead
verify_fix confirms schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
review.action: Replace the plain CREATE INDEX with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (run outside a transaction block) to avoid blocking writers.

review.summary: The single-statement UPDATE backfilling ~900k NULL notes runs as one 3.5s transaction that stalls concurrent writers for over 3.1s, exceeding both the 2000ms transaction and 50ms writer-stall thresholds.
evidence: Original migration: longest_transaction_ms=3483, concurrent writer max_stall_ms=3172
Batched fix: longest_transaction_ms=91, concurrent writer max_stall_ms=30
verify_fix reports schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true
review.action: Replace the single UPDATE with the batched DO-block backfill (5,000 rows per commit) before merging.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes is fast and non-blocking (67ms txn, 1-2ms writer stall) but irreversibly destroys the 99,769 non-null `notes` values with no backup, which is a DATA_LOSS per the rubric even though lock/duration/query metrics are all clean.
evidence: Pre-migration: notes has 99,769 non-null rows out of 1,000,000 (9.98%) that are permanently discarded by the DROP COLUMN.
Migration itself is fast/safe on its own: duration_ms=1 (original run) / 67ms (with archive), concurrent writer max_stall_ms=1-2, well under the 50ms/2000ms thresholds.
Query recent_orders_for_customer.sql unaffected: 0.037ms→0.058ms, still Bitmap Index Scan, 0 seq-scanned rows post-migration — no QUERY_REGRESSION.
review.fixed_migration:
-- Archive the data before dropping so it is recoverable if 'unused' turns out to be wrong
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders_notes_archive AS
SELECT id AS order_id, notes
FROM orders
WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;

ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes;
-- orders_notes_archive can be exported/retained per data-retention policy, then dropped once confirmed unneeded
review.action: Before merging, archive the 99,769 non-null notes values to a backup table (or export) so the drop is recoverable, since verify_fix confirms the archived version is still flagged as lossy for the orders.notes column and adds an extra orders_notes_archive table (schema not identical to a bare drop) — get explicit sign-off that this data is truly disposable before running the plain DROP COLUMN.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE customers ALTER COLUMN email TYPE varchar(20) silently truncates 10,001 of 20,000 emails (longest is 21 chars) with no error, and post-migration the customer_by_email lookup for a truncated address returns 0 rows instead of 1.
evidence: lossy_changes reported: customers.email longest existing value was 21 chars, column now varchar(20)
10001/20000 seeded emails exceed 20 chars per planner data facts, all silently truncated with USING left(email,20)
customer_by_email query: rows_returned=1 before migration vs rows_returned=0 after, for the same lookup value
review.action: Do not run this migration as written; first identify and remediate the 10,001 customers with emails longer than 20 characters (truncate deliberately with sign-off, store the full value elsewhere, or raise the UI limit) before attempting to narrow the column, since no migration can both narrow to varchar(20) and preserve those values.

review.summary: Adding the FK constraint inline validates all 1M rows of orders under a ShareRowExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers 76ms (>50ms threshold); use NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT instead.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max_stall_ms=76 (>50ms threshold) with orders held under ShareRowExclusiveLock
constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table=true in original simulation
Fixed version (NOT VALID then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT): max_stall_ms=3, lock reduced to ShareUpdateExclusiveLock, schema_equivalent=true
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2 FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2;
review.action: Replace the inline ADD CONSTRAINT with NOT VALID followed by a separate VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statement to avoid blocking writers during validation.

review.summary: orders_customer_id_idx is not actually unused: dropping it forces recent_orders_for_customer.sql to seq-scan all 1,000,000 orders rows (0.037ms → 13.374ms, ~361x slower), so the index report is wrong and this DROP INDEX must not ship.
evidence: Post-migration query plan changed from Bitmap Index Scan to Seq Scan reading 1,000,002 rows (seq-scan threshold is 100,000)
Execution time rose from 0.037ms to 13.374ms, ~361x slower (threshold is 5x)
Migration itself is cheap/safe: 3ms duration, 1ms max writer stall, no locks held on user tables
review.action: Do not drop orders_customer_id_idx; re-verify the 'unused index' report against production pg_stat_user_indexes since this index is actively required by recent_orders_for_customer.sql, and if it truly must go, add a supporting composite index (e.g. (customer_id, created_at)) built CONCURRENTLY before dropping the old one.

review.summary: The new index is on raw `status`, but the weekly report filters on `lower(status)`, so it still seq-scans all 2M rows (105ms, no speedup) — build an expression index matching the actual query instead.
evidence: Before and after migration, weekly_paid_report still does Seq Scan over rows_seq_scanned=2000001 (105.2ms vs 101.1ms) — index unused
Migration itself is safe to apply: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY caused only 1ms writer stall, no locks blocking
Fixed migration using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ... (lower(status), created_at) WHERE lower(status)='paid' drops execution to 14.7ms with 0 rows scanned via Bitmap Index Scan
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_created_at_idx ON orders (lower(status), created_at) WHERE lower(status) = 'paid';
review.action: Replace the plain status index with the verified expression index on lower(status) (partial on 'paid', including created_at) so the weekly report query can actually use it.

review.summary: Narrowing customers.email to varchar(40) rewrites the table but is fast enough on the 20k-row customers table to stay under all hazard thresholds.
evidence: Concurrent writer max stall 33ms (<50ms threshold) during the ALTER's AccessExclusiveLock
Longest transaction 38ms (<2000ms threshold), total migration duration 51ms
No data loss: max email length well under 40 chars, 0 rows dropped, both affected queries still use Index/Bitmap Index Scan with 0 seq-scanned rows before and after
review.action: Ship as-is, but re-check stall time if the production customers table is dramatically larger than the 20k-row shadow seed, since the rewrite cost scales with table size.

review.summary: The migration as written fails outright because 90% of existing orders.notes values are NULL, so ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN notes SET NOT NULL aborts with "column contains null values" and never reaches the desired end state.
evidence: simulate_migration reproduced the exact error: 'column "notes" of relation "orders" contains null values' with 0 rows changed
~900k/1,000,000 orders rows have notes IS NULL per seed data, guaranteeing this failure on any real run

A batched backfill-only rewrite (10k-row batches, per-batch COMMIT) measured 0 lock_timeout_errors and a max writer stall of 3ms with longest single transaction 47ms, well under the 2000ms/50ms thresholds
review.action: Do not run this migration as-is; backfill orders.notes in small batched/committed transactions first, then use the NOT VALID CHECK + VALIDATE + SET NOT NULL pattern, and re-verify writer-stall/lock_timeout numbers on the ADD CONSTRAINT and VALIDATE CONSTRAINT steps specifically before shipping, since repeated measurements showed those two steps (not the backfill) intermittently tripped the concurrent writer's lock_timeout even though stalls stayed under 6ms.
